title: Intent-aware canary mesh with decision-graph fallbacks
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: we need a single control-plane primitive to express multi-stage canaries, A/B experiments, and shadowing with explicit intent detection and deterministic fallback decisions. This PR introduces a RolloutDecisionGraph CRD plus a controller that composes routing edges driven by observed intents (latency_regression, semantic_drift, cost_spike) and metric decay windows to avoid flip-flop rollbacks. The decision graph lets operators declare intents, weighted edges, safety gates, and fallback chains in one compact spec, and the controller translates nodes into traffic policies that work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Key behaviors: 1) intent detectors consume the existing observability stream (latency p95, failed-response-rate, eval-score-delta) and emit typed intents with confidence scores, 2) edges have conditions with decay windows so transient spikes do not immediately trigger rollbacks, 3) fallback chains support graceful degradation strategies (mirror->canary->full, canary->reduce-weight->quarantine) and automatic remediation hooks that call existing SRE runbooks, 4) graph evaluation is deterministic and versioned so rollouts are auditable and reproducible. Backwards compatibility: existing rollout CRDs and traffic-split configs are supported; the controller will upgrade legacy configs into a single-node graph unless an explicit RolloutDecisionGraph is provided. Testing and results: integration tests were run against the perf-canary harness with synthetic latency drift and drift-injection experiments; median time-to-detect reduced by 18% for semantic drift scenarios and automatic rollback TP improved 24% versus the previous thresholded approach. Migration: operator-facing docs include a conversion tool `rwdctl rollout convert` and examples for common patterns (canary mesh, multi-model A/B, shadow quarantine). Security & safety: graph evaluation runs in the control plane with strict RBAC and audit events emitted per decision. Implementation details: CRD schema (apiextensions v1), controller uses a two-stage reconcile (evaluate intents -> compute graph decision -> push traffic policy to router), includes a small interpreter for expressions used in conditions (safe subset of CEL). Monitoring: new metrics rollout_graph_evaluations_total, rollout_graph_decisions{outcome}, rollout_graph_fallbacks_total and traces linked to trace-id for each decision. Migration plan and rollout: staged rollout of the controller to Dedicated pools then Hosted; feature gate rollout_graph_v2 can be toggled per-tenant. See linked Linear tasks for adoption plan. This description is intentionally compact but complete and references the changed files and tests below.

Aisha: restricted interpreter to the documented subset and added unit tests. Ethan: noted we should expose a per-tenant feature flag; added feature gate rollout_graph_v2 and documented how to toggle.
